title: Short-burst runways and headroom playbook — hosted API (15m window)
content:
Purpose:
This working playbook documents short-burst (1–15 minute) capacity modeling for Redwood Hosted API. Focus: tokens/sec and QPS headroom targets driven by microbursts (ads/PLG onboarding events, product launches, social spikes). Goal: concrete GPU-slice and prewarm recommendations per region, with a simple cost/backstop tradeoff and an action checklist for incident response teams.

Executive summary (quick):
- Use 15-minute sliding-window 99th/99.9th percentile demand for planning short-burst safety stock (captures multi-request correlated surges).
- Target headroom = max(absolute_capacity_buffer, percentile_buffer): default = max(40% of 99th-window demand, enough GPUs to cover 5 additional simultaneous large-model requests). This optimizes outage risk vs. committed cost for Hosted API.
- Focus GPU families: H100 (new pools), A100-80GB (stable baseline), and a small T4 pool for small-embedding/low-cost fallbacks.
- Recommend region-level prewarm pools sized to 95th percentile 15-min demand + 30% runway for NA and EU; APAC uses smaller prewarm with cross-region failover due to lower SLA-bound customers.

Assumptions and inputs:
- Request size distribution (tokens per request): P10=60, median=320, P90=1,200, tail P99=4,500 tokens.
- Average tokens/sec per QPS varies by model family; baseline conversion used: small chat model = 60 tokens/sec per 1 QPS (short responses), large chat (context-heavy) = 400 tokens/sec per 1 QPS. We model mixed workload: 60% small, 30% medium (200 t/s per QPS), 10% large.
- GPU throughput (tokens/sec sustained, approximate): H100-giant: 120k t/s for small model shapes, 42k t/s for 4k-context large-chat; A100-80GB: 70k t/s small, 28k t/s large; T4: 8k t/s (embeddings/low-cost). These are conservative and assume 16-bit quantized kernels.
- KV/cache hit ratio effect: 25% median hit reduces token work by ~18% on aggregate; model this as multiplicative reduction when estimating capacity.
- Warm-up overhead: H100 pools require ~40–60s to reach full throughput when scaling new instances (driver init + CUDA warmup). Treat cold-start as 0 tokens for first 20s, 50% throughput at 20–40s, full after 60s.

Demand model and projections (15-minute sliding windows):
We ran synthetic replay (see linked Confluence) based on last 18 months of ingress traces with injected campaign spikes. Representative 15-minute-window percentiles (tokens/sec aggregate, global):
- Median(15m): 48k t/s global
- P90(15m): 123k t/s global
- P99(15m): 312k t/s global
- P99.9(15m): 580k t/s global (very rare coordinated spikes)
By region (P99 15m demand estimate, tokens/sec):
- NA: 190k t/s (dominant, ~61% of global)
- EU: 82k t/s (~26%)
- APAC: 40k t/s (~13%)

Headroom targets (recommendation):
- Operating policy: keep prewarmed capacity to handle 95th-99th range and maintain an elastic cold-backstop for 99.9th. Specific targets:
  - NA: prewarm = P95(15m) + 30% buffer => target prewarm = 250k t/s; guaranteed safety stock GPUs = enough to cover additional 2 large-model concurrent requests (approx +60k t/s).
  - EU: prewarm = P95 + 25% => 110k t/s with safety stock +30k t/s.
  - APAC: prewarm = P90 + 20% => 70k t/s, rely on cross-region failover for extreme tails.
- Translate to GPU counts (rounded up):
  - NA: 250k t/s target -> H100 slice equivalents: ~3.0 H100-full machines (assume 80k effective t/s per machine at mixed workload) -> recommend 4 H100 nodes prewarmed (one spare). If using A100: ~4 A100 nodes + 1 spare.
  - EU: 110k t/s -> 2 H100 or 3 A100 (recommend 3 A100 or 2 H100).
  - APAC: 70k t/s -> 1 H100 or 2 A100.
- Safety-stock (short-burst) policy: maintain 1–2 GPU spares per region (H100 preferred), plus an emergency cross-region pool of 4 GPUs preallocated for <30min bursts.

Prewarm sizing and scaling rules (practical playbook):
- Maintain a small continuous prewarm for each pool equal to 10% of hourly peak to reduce cold starts; scale to target prewarm when hourly trend > P90 for last 30 minutes.
- Scale-up hysteresis: require 3 consecutive 5-minute windows trending above threshold before expanding prewarm to avoid oscillation.
- Rapid-oncall action: if 15-min window exceeds P99 and auto-scaler is insufficient (queueing/latency breach), manually trigger emergency prewarm script (infra/ops runbook) that pulls 4x faster than baseline scaler. Documented in linked_artifacts.

Cost roughing (monthly backlog estimate):
- Example cost assumptions (on-demand equivalent): H100 ~ $28/hr, A100-80GB ~ $9/hr, T4 ~ $1.2/hr.
- Estimated monthly incremental cost for recommended prewarm (regional split): NA(4 H100 prewarmed 24/7) = 4 * 28 * 24 * 30 ≈ $80.6k/month. EU(3 A100) ≈ 3 * 9 * 24 * 30 ≈ $19.4k/month. APAC(2 A100) ≈ $12k/month. Total prewarm bill ≈ $112k/month.
- Note: Dedicated or reserved capacity contracts will materially lower committed cost; these numbers are for evaluation only.

Fallback & graceful degradation matrix:
- When cross-region failover triggered, reduce model class served in fallback tier (large -> medium -> small) preserving core PLG paths; degrade sampling/temperature features to reduce tokens/sec where acceptable.
- If prewarm depleted and queueing grows >20s p99, switch to degraded response mode (fast small-chat fallback) per-route via routing policy. This preserves availability at expense of quality.

Simulation notes and sensitivity:
- Simulation with KV-hit toggles: +15% KV hit reduces NA prewarm by ~40k t/s -> allows dropping 1 H100 in NA pool.
- Warm-up penalty simulation: H100 cold-start can create a 60–120s hole if autoscaler triggers many nodes simultaneously. Avoid scaling from 0; maintain small hot pool.
- Overprovision cost vs outage cost curve included in Confluence link (long-tail risk analysis). Short summary: reducing headroom from 40% -> 20% saves ~45% prewarm cost but increases P99.9 outage probability 4x in simulations.

Operational runbook (step-by-step when 15m window breaches thresholds):
1) Alert (automatic): metric: 15m-window tokens/sec > prewarm_target * 0.95 -> paging to infra-oncall.
2) Infra-oncall: verify KV-hit and model-mix via quick-runbook dashboard.
3) If autoscaler hasn't added nodes within 60s -> execute emergency_prewarm.sh with region argument (script w/ 3-minute cooldown).
4) Trigger routing policy: divert new requests to fallback model family on non-critical routes.
5) After 15 minutes of reduced load, evaluate whether to keep emergency nodes for 30–60 more minutes (cost vote).

Open questions and TODOs (short):
- Verify throughput numbers for newly onboarded 8-bit quantized variants (A100 vs H100 delta). Action: Jin to run kernel microbenchmarks (JIRA-INFRA-990).
- Add per-route cost attribution to console to allow product teams to understand headroom tradeoffs. (Miguel).
- Validate cross-region cold-network implications for failover (APAC -> NA) under TCP-level constraints.

Appendix: quick numbers snapshot (rounded):
- Global 15m P99 demand: 312k t/s -> recommended prewarm pool ~ 320–360k t/s aggregate with regional split per above.
- Target spare GPUs regionally: NA: 4 prewarm H100 + 1 spare; EU: 3 A100 + 1 spare; APAC: 2 A100 + 1 spare; emergency global pool: 4 GPUs.

Notes to reviewers: this is a working doc. I intentionally weighted H100 for short-burst headroom because of higher throughput/warmup tradeoffs; alternative is more A100 nodes with higher parallelism. Please comment inline and link sim runs you used for local testing.

Action items (owner tags):
- Priya: finalize prewarm scripts and emergency scaling repo entry (infra/preswarm/).
- Jin: microbench throughput matrix for quantized v2 models (JIRA-INFRA-990).
- Miguel: cost/contract scenarios with committed discounts (finance loop).
- Aisha: add per-region network failover verification tests to perf CI.
summary: Working playbook for sizing short-burst 15-minute-runway prewarm pools for Redwood Hosted API. Contains assumptions, region-level targets, GPU mapping, cost estimate, runbook steps, and action items.
